sections.title: From a neuron to agents that communicate
teaching: A **single neuron** multiplies its inputs by weights and adds the products into one number. A **neural network** combines these operations into layers, turning one input vector into a decision vector.

An **LLM** processes fifteen vectors through successive layers and predicts a sixteenth vector, a probability distribution over the next token. An **agentic system** joins whole LLMs into a graph that outlines, writes, criticizes, revises and finalizes the response.
The critic and reviser form a loop so a revised draft can be evaluated again. The agents communicate in English and can work in other human languages and computer languages.
**Inference uses inner products**, while learning uses **SGD and dynamic programming**. Inference processes current inputs with learned weights, while learning changes the weights to reduce error.

sections.title: Parallel heads and successive layers
teaching: **Predicting the next word is difficult**, so an LLM uses many layers to develop its input representations. Each layer transforms the vectors produced by the preceding layer.

Within a layer, **heads work in parallel as different experts**. Their contributions are combined into new representations, and the next layer repeats the process with those representations. Heads contribute within one stage, while layers provide successive stages.

sections.title: A dynamical rule across time and depth
teaching: A **dynamical system** applies a rule to its state and feeds the resulting state back in. In the oscillator, position is updated using the old velocity, then velocity is updated using that new position. Repeating the rule produces oscillation.

In **Jordan’s recurrent network**, plan and state units feed a hidden layer, output returns to state units, and self-connections preserve a fading trace. The weights are reused over time, so recent outputs affect the next output.

An **LLM** transforms vectors through successive layers, so depth plays the role of time. Following one number through the layers gives a changing curve. Each layer has its own weights, unlike the same rule reused across time in the oscillator and recurrent network.
The small stock-return graph traces Small, Medium and Large series fluctuating over the same period, another example of quantities changing over time.
issues: This deck dates the Jordan network to 1986, while Lecture17 used 1985. The notes prioritize the mechanism and retain the source discrepancy here.
An embedded Small/Medium/Large stock-return graph appears near the oscillator. It is described only as time-varying trajectories, because the deck supplies no market mechanism or numerical argument.

sections.title: One prediction task for different sequences
teaching: An **LLM** receives fifteen vectors and predicts the following one. The vectors can represent words in a sentence, frames of a spectrogram, patches of a picture, or amino acids in the **insulin B chain**.

The picture is divided into sixteen patches, with fifteen given and the bottom-right patch left to predict. In the protein example the next residue is Y. The original materials differ, but all are represented as **sequences of vectors**.
issues: The N beside the folded protein marks its amino end, not an answer in the missing slot. The speaker notes identify the next residue as Y.

sections.title: Which sequences can be English words?
teaching: One-syllable words like Don, mat and fish follow a **consonant, vowel, consonant** pattern. Clusters are allowed **before and after the vowel** only in certain orders, so split, flat, desk and help are words while *sblit, *lfat, *desb and *hepl are impossible, with the order mirroring around the vowel.

A **long word is a chain of syllables**, each obeying the same rules. t·l is fine across a break in At·lan·tic, but **tl cannot start a syllable**, so *tlantic is impossible, and ng can end a syllable but never start one.

sections.title: Guessing the next letter reveals phonotactic knowledge
teaching: Guessing the **next letter** of a word start shows **phonotactic knowledge**. After a vowel, as in **ra_**, almost anything can follow. At the start of a word the choices narrow, to **l, r or a vowel** after sp_, b_ and f_, and to **only a vowel** after skr_ and m_.

Each item also has an impossible continuation, such as *spn, *kt, *skrl or *mb. **Guessing the next letter is predicting x₁₆**, so a **GPT** trained only on this game learns English sounds and spelling, with a broad distribution after ra_ and a sharply peaked one after skr_.
issues: The visible example is ra_ but the speaker notes discuss fa_. Both illustrate the source’s broad post-vowel choices.
